A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MicroMix and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched across v1 Appendices A-C and v2 Appendices A-D despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, perplexity, code-generation, mathematical-reasoning, ablation, and GPU-efficiency results, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and efficiency results, including additional Mixtral, KV-cache, bit-width sensitivity, and decoding evaluations.

M1.justification: The threshold-based channel allocation, offline absolute-mean sorting, MXFP4/6/8 formats, and fused reorder-and-quantize procedure remain. v2 explicitly incorporates INT4 KV-cache quantization into the inference pipeline (Appendix D.2 and Figure 12), whereas v1's Figure 7 describes FlashInfer cache/attention processing without this quantization component.

E1.justification: v2 adds MBPP/MBPP+ code evaluation and MATH, while removing CN Middle School 24. C4 replaces Human-Eval in the calibration-dataset study (v1 Table 5 versus v2 Table 12). Human-Eval+ was already evaluated in v1 Figure 8; the standard zero-shot, MMLU, and WikiText2 coverage remains.

E2.justification: FlatQuant and INT6 enter the main accuracy/perplexity comparison. On retained code benchmarks, Bitsandbytes INT8 replaces Atom. v2 adds a CUTLASS comparison for small GEMMs and replaces the earlier TensorRT end-to-end comparisons with HuggingFace FP16/Bitsandbytes INT8 and Atom/QuaRot comparisons. TensorRT remains in the single-kernel evaluation.

E3.justification: QUIK's stated high-precision feature count changes from 128 to 256, and its quantization changes from the earlier symmetric/grouped description to asymmetric per-token quantization; this does not establish that results were rerun. v2 adds group-64 INT4 KV-cache tests, Mixtral-8x7B evaluation, small-GEMM sweeps, and RTX PRO 6000 decoding tests. The RTX 5090 whole-model comparison changes from batch size 32 to 8/12.

E4.justification: v2 adds layer-wise MSE comparisons (Figure 1c), fused-versus-separate operation measurements (Figure 5), KV-cache accuracy tests (Table 10), and average-bit-width sensitivity (Table 13). Calibration robustness is revised. Conversely, v1's cross-GPU dequantization diagnostic is removed, and its separate FP4/FP6/FP8 runtime breakdown is reduced to aggregate GEMM time.

E5.justification: Both retain mean/min-max reporting for the 32-sample precision-allocation study and latency ranges associated with different precision allocations. Neither reports added random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Many retained results change: MicroMix's Llama3.1-8B MMLU score changes from 58.47 to 62.65, while its Math-7B MMLU-STEM score changes from 77.1 to 66.5. FP16 WikiText2 baselines also change: 5.60 to 6.24 for Llama and 4.46 to 5.02 for Qwen. Numerous benchmark, cache, sensitivity, and efficiency entries are added. These are reported result revisions, not necessarily same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The INT8 error bound and quantization-threshold formula are retained. v2 adds explicit channel-partition equations and a sequence-dependent FlatQuant bit-cost definition. Its new Equation 10 ends the G8 slice at p8 times I rather than I, making the stated partition inconsistent with assigning all remaining channels.

C1.justification: The abstract shifts from competitive accuracy and acceleration over TensorRT-FP8 to near-FP16 accuracy at approximately five bits, lossless Qwen2.5-32B Base/Coder/Math accuracy, and 2.29-3.38x acceleration over TensorRT-FP16. The introduction additionally claims decoding advantages over INT4 baselines on RTX PRO 6000. These materially strengthen accuracy claims and change the headline efficiency comparison.

C2.justification: v1 interprets E3M2 as substantially preferable for MXFP6; v2 interprets all four format combinations as similarly effective and attributes this robustness to exponent/mantissa-aware thresholds. v2 also discusses why more bits need not yield higher accuracy and removes the earlier FP6 runtime-bottleneck discussion. The central adaptivity and calibration-stability interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds substantial baseline bit-width accounting, including scale overhead, QUIK's Down-proj treatment, and FlatQuant transformation matrices with sequence length 100. FlatQuant and KV-cache settings are documented. However, v1's explicit default calibration recipe of 32 WikiText2 sequences of length 2048 and its Qwen-specific QuaRot workaround disappear. The existing calibration-time/memory table is largely relocated, not newly introduced.

R1.justification: v2 expands the post-training quantization background and adds citations including SqueezeLLM, OmniQuant, SpinQuant, DuQuant, and FlatQuant, while dropping Agile-Quant. The central positioning against fixed-allocation mixed-precision methods and existing microscaling research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The algorithm explanation changes from a Q1-Q3 structure to a permutation, threshold, and offline-assignment narrative. Results and efficiency discussions are extensively rewritten. Related work, transformer integration, model-cost information, and calibration results move between the main text and appendices. Author and conference-header information also changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column conference layout. The overview becomes a multipanel figure, kernel schematics are merged, code-result bars become a table, and the component-runtime table is transposed and aggregated. New experimental displays and a per-layer bit-width figure appear, while the earlier transformer-block efficiency plot is removed.

improvement.justification: The added FlatQuant/INT6 comparisons, KV-cache tests, decoding measurements, and baseline accounting strengthen the evaluation. However, v2 removes the TensorRT end-to-end comparison and explicit calibration recipe, introduces an inconsistent partition equation, and claims lossless 32B Math accuracy without corresponding results: Table 3 evaluates Math-7B and shows substantial MMLU-STEM degradation. These substantive gains and losses leave the net direction of overall quality unclear.
